name: The Classic Maya
title: Social Hierarchy of the Classic Maya: From Holy Lord to Captive

tiers.name: Holy lords and overlords
tiers.you: You are a holy lord: you stand between your people and the gods, offer your own blood in ritual, lead your warriors in war and record your deeds on carved stelae, but a defeat could make you another king’s captive.
tiers.kid: Each Maya kingdom had a “holy lord”, a king who led its rituals and its wars.
tiers.rise: Kings were born to their thrones, but war could unmake them: in 648 Yuknoom Ch’een II of Calakmul captured B’ajlaj Chan K’awiil of Dos Pilas and restored him as his vassal, and in 738 Copán’s king Waxaklajuun Ub’aah K’awiil was captured and beheaded by his own vassal, the ruler of Quiriguá.
tiers.why: Each kingdom was ruled by a holy lord, the k’uhul ajaw, who stood between his people and the gods.

tiers.name: Nobles
tiers.term: ajaw ("lord"), sajal ("feared one", a subordinate lord), ch'ok ("youth", a young noble)
tiers.you: You were born into a noble lineage: you live in a stone house near the city centre, wear jade, fight in your lord’s wars and hope that a powerful patron will give you an office at court.
tiers.kid: Maya nobles lived in stone houses near the centre of their city, wore jade and served at the king’s court.
tiers.rise: Noble rank came by birth into a noble lineage. Within it a man rose from office to office under the sponsorship of a higher lord and by taking captives in war, while a lord captured in battle could be sacrificed.
tiers.why: Below the kings stood a hereditary nobility of royal kin and great families.

tiers.name: Scribes and priests
tiers.term: aj tz'ib ("he of the writing"), aj k'uhuun
tiers.you: You were born to a noble family and trained to write: you paint books on bark paper, compose the texts carved on your king’s stelae and help keep the calendar of the rituals.
tiers.kid: Maya scribes came from noble families and painted books and wrote the words carved on stone monuments.
tiers.rise: Scribal and priestly learning passed within noble families; a scribe’s skill could win him honour at court, and some signed their names to their work.
tiers.why: Writing and ritual knowledge belonged to the nobility, and commoners could not read.

tiers.name: Craftsmen and traders
tiers.you: You work at a craft such as pottery or stone tools, or carry cacao and cotton cloth on your back along the trade routes, where cacao beans serve as money.
tiers.kid: Maya craftspeople carved stone and jade and painted fine pots, and traders used cacao beans as money.
tiers.rise: Skill could bring a craftsman to the court’s notice, and enterprising commoners could become influential; on 16th-century evidence, long-distance trade belonged to the nobles, while most traders worked locally.
tiers.why: Specialists made the goods on which the courts, and the trade between kingdoms, depended.

tiers.name: Commoners
tiers.you: You farm maize, beans and squash near your house of poles and thatch, bury your dead beneath its floor, pay taxes to the nobles in maize and game, and go to war when you are called.
tiers.kid: Most Maya were farmers who grew maize, beans and squash and lived in houses with thatched roofs.
tiers.rise: Birth fixed most lives, but commoners could advance by proving themselves as outstanding warriors, and skilled and enterprising commoners could become influential. Drought, war and the collapse of the 9th century drove many from their land.
tiers.why: The great majority were commoners: farmers, labourers and servants, and also craftsmen and a few minor officials.

tiers.name: Captives and the enslaved
tiers.you: You were taken in a raid and now belong to the warrior who captured you; if you are of high rank you may be kept for sacrifice, and if not, you will be put to work.
tiers.kid: Prisoners taken in war were made to work for their captors, and some were sacrificed to the gods.
tiers.rise: Most of the captives the inscriptions name were sacrificed; a few lords were released as vassals, and the fate of lesser captives is little known.
tiers.why: Warfare filled the lowest rank with captives.
